wins: Rapidly identified exposed services through initial scanning, confirming attack surface within first 5 minutes.
Documented useful reconnaissance data that can seed future automation (service versions, banner info).
fails: Unable to obtain initial foothold despite 15 mentor interventions, indicating weakness in exploitation chaining.
Repeated failure to bypass account lockout controls when brute-forcing SSH, halting progress before privilege escalation.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance executed effectively, but repeated exploitation and persistence attempts stall before success; need refined credential handling and lateral movement techniques.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Frequent SSH authentication failures leading to lockouts and no pivot opportunity.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner detected
skill_cards.then_action: Run SSH enumeration with nmap scripts

skill_cards.if_condition: When HTTP service returns login/portal page with forms
skill_cards.then_action: Execute targeted directory and credential fuzzing with gobuster and Burp Intruder

memory_ops.reason: High reliability in initial reconnaissance to confirm SSH presence.

next_experiments.title: Credential handling refinement
next_experiments.description: Introduce adaptive throttle logic for SSH brute-force attempts and rotate credential sets to avoid lockouts.

next_experiments.title: Web authentication attack chain
next_experiments.description: Expand HTTP scanning to include authenticated session reuse via captured cookies to bypass brute-force limits.
